en.title: Earliest Day of Consecutive Occupancy
en.description:
N houses stand in a row, and one house is occupied each day according to the permutation house. Output the earliest day on which at least M consecutive houses are occupied, counting from day 1.

The standard input/output, examples, and tests are written by CSWork; ranges marked "this site" are judging conventions and are not claimed to be original interview limits.
en.input: The first line contains N M (this site's test range: 1≤M≤N≤100000); the second line contains a permutation of 1..N, giving the house occupied on each day.
en.output: Output the answer as described; results for multiple queries are separated by spaces, in order.
en.explanation: Example 1: only 1 house is required, so day 1 already satisfies it. Example 2: houses 1 and 3, occupied on the first two days, are not yet consecutive; on day 3, filling in 2 makes 1, 2, 3 consecutively occupied, so the answer is 3. Example 3: all 4 houses must be consecutive, so you must wait until day 4.
hints: Record each occupied run's length at its two endpoints. When adding position x, read the run lengths of its left and right neighbors, combine them into a new run, and update its two outer endpoints.
